title: Fano atoms are handles
claim: (1) Splice lemma: if a graph A has a vertex x of degree three with genus(A - x) = genus(A), then splicing A at x into any connected graph R at a vertex of degree three, along any bijection of the three edges, has genus genus(A) + genus(R). The proof is a face-tracing identity at the 3-edge cut (genus(G) = genus(G1) + genus(G2) + D/2, with D read off three permutations in S3) together with the fact that a face turning back across a cut edge costs that side a handle. Without the hypothesis additivity fails: K3,3 spliced with K3,3 has genus 1. (2) Genus formula: the Heawood graph satisfies the hypothesis at every vertex and planar pieces add no genus, so the incidence graph of a connected 3-regular triple system with distinct points per line that is not 2-colourable has genus equal to its number of Heawood braces (Fano atoms) when every other brace is planar, and in general the sum of its braces' genera when every non-planar brace satisfies the hypothesis (the trisum of three cubes does). (3) Minimal maps: if both sides of a 3-edge splice satisfy the hypothesis, the minimum-genus rotation systems of the splice are exactly the compatible pairs of minimum-genus rotation systems of the sides, half of all pairs. In a three-fold space with planar glue both sides of every tight cut satisfy it, so every minimum-genus embedding is a connected sum of Heawood maps (one per Fano atom) and planar maps of the glue, and their number is the product over braces divided by 2 per tight cut (16, 128, 1024 for one, two, three atoms without glue). (4) The Fano plane's space is the Heawood map, unique up to symmetry and chiral; its dual is K7 on the torus, whose 14 triangles are the 7 points and the 7 lines of the Fano plane, each class forming a Fano plane on the 7 faces.
failure_conditions: A rotation system violating the face-tracing identity, or an entry of the permutation table contrary to the proof.
A splice of the Heawood graph whose genus differs from genus(R) + 1, or a three-fold space with planar glue whose genus differs from its number of Heawood braces.
A minimum-genus embedding of a three-fold space with planar glue that is not a connected sum of Heawood maps and planar maps, or a count of minimum-genus rotation systems different from the formula.
A second torus map of the Heawood graph up to symmetry, or a dual that is not K7 with two Fano colour classes.
foundation_claim_scope: Orientable genus and minimum-genus rotation systems of splices of graphs along three edges and of incidence graphs of three-fold spaces; the knot reading through the duality of SPACE-SELECTION-20261030-001C. Non-orientable genus and embeddings above the minimum genus are not treated.

validation.status: checked: permutation table exhaustive; face-tracing identity on 1200 random cases; Heawood genus, rigidity, torus maps, orbit, chirality and dual; splice lemma on seven graphs and two bijections, K3,3 failure; all 128 minimum-genus embeddings of the 13-point space standard; genus formula on six spaces up to the 43-point twisted cube; controls fire; no human or external review
validation.novelty: classical inputs: Euler's formula for rotation systems, minor monotonicity of genus, Battle-Harary-Kodama-Youngs (disconnected graphs); the face-permutation calculus is in the spirit of Stahl's permutation-partition pairs; the Heawood map and K7 on the torus are classical. No overlap found (candidate local delta) in a bounded search for the splice lemma with the vertex-deletion hypothesis, the genus formula and the classification of minimum-genus embeddings of three-fold spaces
